text:
maria: Quick heads-up — profiler shows an unusual prefill slowdown when serving long-context FP8 models. TTFT for the first token is fine but decode TPS drops ~20% after ~8k tokens. Link: https://internal.perf/reports/1798 (screenshots attached) :eyes:
chen: can you paste the perf breakdown? is this happening on single-node or multi-node pools? :thinking:
maria: single dedicated pool (a100s). here's the hot path from the flamegraph:
```
prefill_attn_kernel_fp8_global  48%
dequantize_path  22%
kv_eviction_sync 12%
other 18%
```
Seems we fall back to the dequantize_path mid-prefill for some layers after KV eviction pressure.
kevin: hmm eviction sync at 12% is suspicious. are we evicting per-sample or per-microbatch?
sam: we changed the eviction heuristic last month (PR #4456) to be more aggressive to avoid OOM on 24k contexts. could be related.
maria: PR noted: switch to LRU with chunked segments. I can repro locally with longctx=12k, microbatch=8.
chen: does this repro with INT8 or 4-bit quant too or only FP8?
maria: FP8 is the worst. INT8 shows milder impact (~7% TPS drop). 4-bit hybrid has different profile: more compute but less eviction since KV smaller.
julia: are kernels switching? Maybe kernel selector picks a prefill-optimized kernel initially but for decode we want a different path. We added a fallback in kernel_selector for precision mismatch last quarter.
kevin: can you run the microprobe to show kernel ids used in prefill vs decode? simple script: 
```bash
INVOKE_PROF=1 ./bin/serve --model xlp8 --trace kernels > kernels.log
```
post logs please.
maria: pasted kernel ids — prefill uses kernel id 0x10 (fp8_global_prefill), decode for later tokens switches to 0x1f (emulated_dequant_decode).
sam: That 0x1f was introduced as fallback for small-slice sizes where fused FP8 kernels were unstable. If evictions create fragmented KV segments, slice sizes change and selector favors emulated path.
chen: interesting. So fragmentation -> different slice -> kernel fallback -> dequant path -> TPS drop. makes sense.
julia: short-term: adjust selector thresholds to prefer decode-optimized kernels when streaming flag set. Long-term: reduce KV fragmentation by coalescing segments and avoid eviction per microbatch.
kevin: also check batching heuristics. If we microbatch differently we can keep slice sizes stable across prefill/decode boundary. Try bumping microbatch from 8->12 for stress test.
maria: ran microbatch=12: TPS drop reduced to ~8% (from 20%). Good signal.
sam: PR rollback for #4456 might be needed for certain customers. but let's open a targeted fix first.
maria: filed issue PERF-2987 with repro, flamegraphs, kernel ids, and suggested mitigations. assigned to eng-runtime.
deploy-bot: canary deployed kernel-selector tweak to test pool "dedicated-longctx-3" at 11:02 UTC.
chen: nice, will monitor. can we add an experiment to capture kernel_id timeline per request (small perf cost) for 24h?
julia: yes add opt-in telemetry gated by customer opt-in for dedicated pools. helps root cause.
kevin: action items: 1) rollback aggressive eviction for longctx customers (sam) 2) tweak kernel selector thresholds for streaming (julia) 3) run microbatch tuning sweep (maria) 4) add kernel_id telemetry (chen).
maria: I'll run a benchmark matrix: {precision: [fp8,int8,4bit], context: [4k,8k,12k], microbatch: [8,12,16]}. ETA EOD tomorrow.
sam: planning note: watch for quality regressions when forcing kernels — calibration differences may change output. add evals to perf runs.
chen: exactly. calibration->quantization can change token distributions; include the eval harness.
maria: noted. thanks all :thumbsup: we'll update PERF-2987 with results and next steps.
